newsitem.title: TURKEY: Turkish shares jump 2.84 pct to new record.
newsitem.headline: Turkish shares jump 2.84 pct to new record.

text.p: Istanbul shares rose on Thursday in selective buying which accelerated in the afternoon on news that the new year holiday was extended to five days and payments will be delayed to after the holiday, brokers said.
The IMKB-100 .ISEC closed at a new all-time high of 97,425.62, up 2,690.27 points, or 2.84 percent from Wednesday and compared to a previous record of 94,879.14 on December 20.
In dollar terms, the index stood at 91 cents, up from 89.5 cents on December 20, but down from a $1 record on April 8. The index's end-1995 value was $0.67.
"Purchases were fuelled by afternoon news that the new year holiday was extended. It was seen positive that settlements would be delayed," said Nazmi Sarikaya from Disbank.
The goverment extended the holiday to five days from December 27 to January 2 by declaring December 30 and 31 official holiday in the public sector.
The Exchange administration said afterwards the stock market would be closed on Monday and Tuesday and today's transactions would be settled on January 2, and Friday's transactions on January 3.
Trade volume rose to 14.85 trillion lira from Thursday's 11.70 trillion.
Brokers had earlier said an extended holiday would allow traders to place their funds in repo deals over the holiday due to delayed settlements.

Brokers said activity was led by bluechip utilities and largely state-owned stocks which have a major impact on the market index. Two-day gains totalled 4.01 percent after a 1.28 percent loss in the first two days of the week.

Of the 232 shares traded, gainers outdid losers sharply by 188 to 15 and 29 closed steady. The 85-share industrial index .ISEI leapt 2.31 percent to 104,244.67 and the 15-share financial index .ISEF surged 4.08 percent to 91,640.77.
Top actives were Cukurova Elektrik, up 2,500 lira at 135,000, and Aktas Elektrik, up 4,000 lira to 96,000. Together, they made up 19 percent of the total turnover.
